chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and Tempo Music
title: Morton's circumstances in 1938 and the Library of Congress recordings

blocks.x: had this was before jelly had gotten back into recording wasn't it it was while he was here in 1938

he hadn't recorded for about five or six or seven years yes he came down from new york in 35 and i think he may have recorded once or twice after 32 but i'm not positive of the dates anyhow he'd been out of about five years and he was really on his uppers i could see that the man wasn't making anything he had recorded the library of congress material no he did that during the summer that year of 38 after i i went in there in march 38 and met him first and he had that project was on they were going to do it and during the summer he did a lot of that did you attend some of those sessions no i never did i went up there one day on the invitation from pardon me jelly and lomax over the phone i was at work that day and they called me up and asked me if i wanted to come up there but it was only to talk the machine had broken down so they weren't recording and they just wanted to did lomax take additional notes to those that were recorded oh yes i believe he did i think there are quite a few notes i wondered if it
